GOOGL.rationale: Alphabet delivered a blowout Q2 2026 quarter with revenue of $119.8B (+24% YoY) and GAAP EPS of $9.11, massively beating consensus of $2.88, though the EPS beat was heavily inflated by ~$99B in investment gains (Anthropic, SpaceX IPO). Stripping out investment gains, operating income of $40.77B and operating margin of ~34% remain strong, with Google Cloud surging 82% YoY to $24.8B and a $514B backlog. The balance sheet is a fortress with $242B cash and total equity of $640B. However, the stock sold off 6-7% post-earnings because management raised 2026 capex guidance to $195-205B (from $180-190B), turning free cash flow negative at -$5.8B in Q2 for the first time as a public company. This massive AI spending creates near-term cash flow uncertainty. Valuation is attractive: at $317.69, the trailing P/E of 18.1x is at the absolute bottom of its 365-day range (18.1-39.5x) and P/B of 6.1x is also at the floor of its range (6.1-12.7x), representing a significant discount to recent history. The stock is down ~6.4% over the past quarter. Key risks include antitrust structural remedies (DOJ Chrome/Android divestiture risk), Gemini 3.5 Pro delays, and margin compression from AI compute costs. Berkshire Hathaway's $31B position and Warren Buffett's personal endorsement provide institutional validation. The near-term catalyst is the post-earnings selloff creating a potential buying opportunity at historically cheap multiples, though the capex overhang and negative FCF may keep sentiment depressed near-term.

Alphabet stock fell 6.6% despite crushing Q2 earnings expectations with $9.11 EPS (vs. $2.88 expected) and $119.8B revenue. The decline was driven by investor concerns over massive AI capital investments of $195-205B this year, which have turned the company's free cash flow negative at -$5.8B in Q2
Alphabet's capex grew 100% year-over-year to $44.9 billion in Q2. Google lifted its full-year spending guide, expecting capital expenditures to range between $195 billion and $205 billion
Google's cloud revenue jumped 82% to $24.8 billion. Cloud backlog totalled $514 billion
Berkshire Hathaway has significantly increased its stake in Alphabet to nearly $31 billion, making it the conglomerate's fifth-largest holding
Ongoing antitrust litigation in the United States and Europe regarding Alphabet's dominance in the advertising technology stack and its default search agreements has reached a critical phase

Google's flagship AI model Gemini 3.5 Pro is months behind its promised June launch date as the company works to improve coding capabilities, raising concerns about competition from OpenAI and Anthropic
